title: Teamwork Works Best With a Team

vocabulary.meaning_en: the person who is in charge of you at work
vocabulary.example: My boss gave me a new project.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a meeting or report where someone checks how well you did
vocabulary.note_en: A work review checks how well you did your job.
vocabulary.example: I have my work review on Monday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a picture that shows numbers, often with lines or bars
vocabulary.example: This chart shows our sales for each month.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the people who watch or listen to a show
vocabulary.example: The audience clapped at the end of the show.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to become lower or smaller
vocabulary.example: The price of bread went down this week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to become higher or bigger
vocabulary.example: I want these numbers to go up.

vocabulary.meaning_en: with the top part at the bottom
vocabulary.example: You are holding the map upside down.

vocabulary.meaning_en: with the top part at the top, the correct way
vocabulary.example: Turn the picture right-side up.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to turn something over quickly
vocabulary.example: Flip the paper over and write your name.

vocabulary.meaning_en: figures; here, how many people watch
vocabulary.example: Our numbers are better this year.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a large printed picture or notice that you put on a wall
vocabulary.example: There is a poster of a cat on the wall.

vocabulary.meaning_en: carefully and with real attention
vocabulary.example: Please think seriously about my idea.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to do what you tried to do
vocabulary.example: If you work hard, you will succeed.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the result of doing well
vocabulary.example: The new show was a big success.

vocabulary.meaning_en: difficult; or with a lot of effort
vocabulary.note_ar: hard ظرف بدون ly. أما hardly فمعناها «بالكاد».
vocabulary.note_en: Hard is also an adverb, with no -ly. "Hardly" means "almost not".
vocabulary.example: This test is hard. I need to work hard.

vocabulary.meaning_en: people working together well as a group
vocabulary.example: Good teamwork helps us finish on time.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a group of people who work or play together
vocabulary.example: Our team has five people.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the one you like best
vocabulary.example: Blue is my favorite color.

vocabulary.meaning_en: pretty and nice to look at (often small things or animals)
vocabulary.example: What a cute little cat!

vocabulary.meaning_en: to feel that something bad may happen
vocabulary.example: Don't worry. Everything will be fine.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an idea of what you are going to do
vocabulary.example: Here's the plan for today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: completely; in every way
vocabulary.example: This is exactly what I need.

vocabulary.meaning_en: liked by many people
vocabulary.example: Football is very popular in my country.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an animal you keep at home
vocabulary.example: Do you have a pet?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to speak very quietly
vocabulary.example: She whispered the answer to me.

fine_lines.title: enough before a noun vs after an adjective
fine_lines.explanation_ar: enough تأتي قبل الاسم (enough cats) لكنها تأتي بعد الصفة (big enough).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Enough comes before a noun (enough cats) but after an adjective (big enough).

examples.sentence: Did I give you enough cats?
Your audience is big, but not big enough.

fine_lines.title: go up vs go down
fine_lines.explanation_ar: go up = يرتفع أو يزيد. go down = ينخفض أو يقل. نستخدمهما مع الأرقام والأسعار.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Go up = become higher or more. Go down = become lower or less. We use them with numbers and prices.

examples.sentence: The temperature goes down at night.

fine_lines.title: succeed vs success
fine_lines.explanation_ar: succeed فعل (ينجح)، success اسم (نجاح)، successful صفة (ناجح).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Succeed is a verb, success is a noun, successful is an adjective.

expressions.meaning_en: It is now the time to work.
expressions.example: It's eight o'clock. Time for work!
Everyone had a review. Now it's time for mine.

expressions.meaning_en: Big, but we need it to be bigger.
expressions.example: The room is nice, but it's not big enough.

expressions.phrase: You really ought to think seriously about ...
expressions.meaning_ar: عليك فعلاً أن تفكر بجدية في ...
expressions.meaning_en: You should think carefully about something.
expressions.example: You really ought to think seriously about your future.

expressions.meaning_en: This is the one I like best.
expressions.example: I like all these books, but this is my favorite.

expressions.phrase: Do you understand what I want?
expressions.meaning_en: Asking if the other person knows what you want.
expressions.example: Do you understand what I want you to do?
You look worried. What's the problem?

expressions.meaning_en: A kind way to tell someone not to be afraid.
expressions.example: Please don't worry. I can help you.

expressions.meaning_en: Used before you explain what you will do.
expressions.example: Here's the plan: we meet at nine and leave at ten.
We have a lot to do. Let's get to work!

grammar.title: If + present simple, will + verb (real conditions)
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم هذا التركيب للحديث عن نتيجة حقيقية أو محتملة: إذا حدث شيء، سيحدث شيء آخر. في جملة if نستخدم المضارع البسيط (look وليس will look)، وفي النتيجة نستخدم will + الفعل. يمكن أن تبدأ الجملة بـ if (مع فاصلة) أو تأتي if في الوسط (بدون فاصلة).
grammar.explanation_en: Use this form to talk about a real or likely result: if one thing happens, another thing will happen. In the if-part use the present simple (look, not will look). In the result part use will + verb. Start with if (and use a comma), or put if in the middle (no comma).
examples: If you look at this chart, you will see something good.
If you work hard, you will succeed.
You will see the problem if you look carefully.

grammar.title: ought to = should (advice)
grammar.explanation_ar: ought to تعني نفس should تقريباً: نصيحة أو الشيء الصحيح الذي يجب فعله. بعدها الفعل في المصدر بدون to إضافية: ought to think. النفي: ought not to (قليل الاستخدام؛ shouldn't أشيع).
grammar.explanation_en: Ought to means almost the same as should: advice, or the right thing to do. Use the base verb after it: ought to think. Negative: ought not to (not common; shouldn't is more usual).
examples: You really ought to think seriously about them.
You ought to drink more water.

questions.question: Complete: "If you look at this chart, you ____ something good."
questions.explanation_ar: في النتيجة نستخدم will + الفعل: will see.
questions.explanation_en: The result part uses will + verb: will see.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
choices: If you will work hard, you succeed.
If you work hard, you will succeed.
If you worked hard, you will succeed.
If you work hard, you succeeding.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد if المضارع البسيط، وفي النتيجة will.
questions.explanation_en: Use the present simple after if, and will in the result.

questions.question: "You ought to think seriously about it." "ought to" means ...
questions.explanation_en: Ought to means about the same as should (advice).

questions.question: The chart is "upside down". What should you do?
questions.explanation_ar: إذا كان مقلوباً نقلبه ليصبح right-side up.
questions.explanation_en: If it's upside down, flip it so it is right-side up.

questions.question: The people who watch a TV show are its ...
questions.explanation_en: The audience is the people who watch.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: "Your audience is big, but not big ____."
questions.explanation_ar: enough تأتي بعد الصفة: big enough.
questions.explanation_en: Enough comes after the adjective: big enough.

questions.question: "I want these numbers to go ____." (We want more people to watch.)
"Teamwork" means ...
questions.explanation_en: Teamwork is people working well together.

questions.question: What do you say when your team does well?
